definitions.gloss: to tidy up; to put in order; to arrange neatly
definitions.explanation: To organize and arrange things so they are neat and orderly. Focuses on arranging items in their proper places rather than cleaning dirt.

examples.japanese: {机|つくえ}の{上|うえ}を{整頓|せいとん}する。
{部屋|へや}を{整頓|せいとん}してから{出|で}かけよう。
examples.english: Let's tidy up the room before going out.

examples.japanese: {本棚|ほんだな}の{本|ほん}をジャンルごとに{整頓|せいとん}した。
examples.english: I organized the books on the shelf by genre.

notes:
A する-verb from {整頓|せいとん}, meaning to arrange things neatly in their proper places. Almost always appears paired with {整理|せいり} in the set phrase {整理|せいり}{整頓|せいとん}, which is ubiquitous in Japanese schools, workplaces, and homes.

TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive — takes を to mark the thing being tidied.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {整理|せいり}{整頓|せいとん} — tidying and organizing (a set phrase)
- {身|み}の{回|まわ}りを{整頓|せいとん}する — to tidy up one's personal space
- {整頓|せいとん}された{部屋|へや} — a well-organized room

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {整理|せいり}する — to organize, sort out (includes discarding unnecessary things)
- {片付|かたづ}ける — to tidy up, put away (more casual, everyday)
- {掃除|そうじ}する — to clean (focuses on removing dirt, not organizing)
